gloss: be hard, severe, difficult; harden, stiffen (the neck, the heart)
summary: קָשָׁה is to be hard: heavy to bear, severe, difficult. Bondage is “hard service” (Exo 1:14), a rough answer is spoken “hard” (1Ki 12:13), a battle or a hand of judgment is hard upon someone (2Sa 2:17; 1Sa 5:7), and a matter “too hard” goes to a higher judge (Deu 1:17). Above all scripture uses it of a will that will not bend: Israel is a people “hard of neck” (Exo 32:9), who “stiffened their neck” and would not hear (2Ki 17:14), and the call is “Do not harden your heart” (Psa 95:8), which Hebrews takes up (Heb 3:8). Arabic qasā, Aramaic and Syriac qšā have the same sense of hard and harsh.

words.gloss: hard: heavy to bear, harsh, severe, difficult; stiff, stubborn
words.summary: Hard in the sense of what presses on or resists someone: heavy labour, harsh words, a severe battle or vision, a matter too difficult; and, in קְשֵׁה עֹרֶף “hard of neck”, a people that will not bend to Yahweh.

senses.gloss: hard, heavy (of labour, service, a yoke)
senses.definition: Of work laid on someone: crushing, wearing them down, the bondage of Egypt or a king’s forced labour, from which rest is a release.

evidence.note: The Egyptians “made their lives bitter בַּעֲבֹדָה קָשָׁה, in mortar and brick”, with all the work they made them do בְּפָרֶךְ, with rigour.
Israel would not listen to Moses “for shortness of spirit and for עֲבֹדָה קָשָׁה”.
“The Egyptians did evil to us and afflicted us and laid on us עֲבֹדָה קָשָׁה.”
“Lighten (הָקֵל) the עֲבֹדָה הַקָּשָׁה of your father and his heavy (כָּבֵד) yoke.”
Yahweh will give Israel rest “from your pain and your turmoil and from the הָעֲבֹדָה הַקָּשָׁה that was laid on you”.

senses.gloss: harsh, rough (of words, a master, a man)
senses.definition: Of speech and of people: hard in dealing with others, rough, unbending, the opposite of soft and gentle.

evidence.note: Joseph “made himself strange to them and spoke קָשׁוֹת with them”.
“The man, the lord of the land, spoke קָשׁוֹת to us.”
Rehoboam answered the people קָשָׁה, forsaking the elders’ counsel to speak them good words (1Ki 12:7).
“Who will tell me if your father answers you קָשָׁה?”
“I am רַךְ, tender, today, though anointed king, and these men, the sons of Zeruiah, are קָשִׁים, harder, than I.”
Nabal was קָשֶׁה וְרַע מַעֲלָלִים, “hard and evil in his doings”, set against his wife, good of understanding.
Egypt given into the hand of אֲדֹנִים קָשֶׁה, a hard master, and a fierce (עַז) king.
Ahijah to Jeroboam’s wife: “I am sent to you with hard news (קָשָׁה).”

senses.gloss: stiff, stubborn (hard of neck, face, heart)
senses.definition: Of a people or a heart: hard as a neck that will not bow to the yoke, refusing to hear and turn; the people’s own rebellion against Yahweh.

evidence.note: At the calf: “I have seen this people, and behold, it is עַם קְשֵׁה עֹרֶף.”
“I will not go up among you, for you are עַם קְשֵׁה עֹרֶף, lest I consume you on the way.”
Moses: “Let my Lord go among us, for it is עַם קְשֵׁה עֹרֶף, and pardon our iniquity.”
“Not for your righteousness is Yahweh giving you this good land, for you are עַם קְשֵׁה עֹרֶף.”
“I know your rebellion (מֶרִי) and your hard neck”, set together.
After each judge died they did not cease “from their stubborn way”, דַּרְכָּם הַקָּשָׁה.
“I knew that you are קָשֶׁה, and your neck an iron sinew and your brow bronze.”
“Sons קְשֵׁי פָנִים, hard of face, and strong of heart.”
Israel will not listen to you, for they will not listen to me: “strong of forehead וּקְשֵׁי לֵב, hard of heart”.

senses.gloss: severe, fierce (of battle, sword, wind, a hand)
senses.definition: Of force: severe, fierce, pressing hard on whoever it falls on.

evidence.note: “The battle was קָשָׁה עַד מְאֹד, very severe, that day, and Abner was struck down.”
The hand of Israel went on, הָלוֹךְ וְקָשָׁה, pressing harder on Jabin, until they cut him off.
Yahweh will punish Leviathan “with his sword, הַקָּשָׁה וְהַגְּדוֹלָה וְהַחֲזָקָה, hard and great and strong”.
“He removed her by his רוּחַ הַקָּשָׁה, in the day of the east wind.”
“Love is strong (עַזָּה) as death, jealousy קָשָׁה, hard, as the grave”: what will not let go.

senses.gloss: hard to bear, grievous (of a vision, a day, a spirit)
senses.definition: Of what befalls a person: grievous, heavy on the spirit.

evidence.note: “A חָזוּת קָשָׁה, a hard vision, has been declared to me”, and the prophet is seized with pangs (Isa 21:3).
“You have made your people see קָשָׁה, hard things; you have made us drink the wine of staggering.”
“Did I not weep for him who was קְשֵׁה יוֹם, hard of day? My soul grieved for the needy.”
Hannah: “I am a woman קְשַׁת רוּחַ, hard of spirit; I have drunk neither wine nor strong drink, but have poured out my soul before Yahweh.”

senses.definition: Of a case at law: too hard for the lesser judges, so brought up to Moses.

evidence.note: “The הַדָּבָר הַקָּשֶׁה they brought to Moses, and every small (קָטֹן) matter they judged themselves.”

evidence.locator: קָשֶׁה → σκληρός, Gen.42.7, Exo.1.14, Exo.6.9, Deu.26.6, Deu.31.27, 1Ki.12.4, 1Ki.12.13, Isa.14.3, Isa.48.4, Sng.8.6 (MACULA alignment)

evidence.note: “This is a σκληρός word; who can hear it?”
“I knew you, that you are a σκληρός man.”
“It is σκληρόν for you to kick against the goads.”
The σκληρά that ungodly sinners have spoken against him.

evidence.locator: עַם קְשֵׁה עֹרֶף → σκληροτράχηλος, Exo.33.3, Exo.33.5, Exo.34.9, Deu.9.6, Deu.9.13 (aligned to עֹרֶף)

evidence.note: Stephen takes up the phrase of Exo 33:5 and Deu 10:16 together: “You σκληροτράχηλοι and uncircumcised in heart and ears, you always resist the holy spirit; as your fathers did, so do you.”

parallels.note: Strong, fierce: anger עָז and wrath קָשָׁתָה; a hard master and a fierce king; love strong as death, jealousy hard as the grave.
Strong, hard: “hard of face and strong of heart”; Yahweh’s sword hard, great and strong.
Heavy: the hard service and the heavy yoke.

opposites.note: Tender, soft: David רַךְ, the sons of Zeruiah קָשִׁים.
Small: the hard matter goes to Moses, the small the judges decide.
Lighten (hiphil הָקֵל), asked of the hard service.

phrases.gloss: a people hard of neck, stiff-necked

words.gloss: be hard, severe, difficult; (hiphil) make hard, harden, stiffen

stems.gloss: be hard, severe; be too difficult

senses.definition: Of anger, a hand, words: to be severe, fierce, pressing hard.

evidence.note: “Cursed be their anger, for it is fierce (עָז), and their wrath, for it is cruel (קָשָׁתָה).”
The men of Ashdod: the ark shall not stay with us, “for his hand קָשְׁתָה, is hard, upon us and upon Dagon our god”.
“The word of the men of Judah was fiercer (וַיִּקֶשׁ) than the word of the men of Israel.”

senses.definition: Of a matter or a duty: to be beyond someone, or to seem hard in their eyes.

evidence.note: “The matter that is too hard (יִקְשֶׁה) for you, bring to me and I will hear it.”
“It shall not seem hard in your eyes (לֹא יִקְשֶׁה בְעֵינֶךָ) when you send him out free from you.”

senses.definition: Of a man in the land under judgment: hard pressed, oppressed by want.

evidence.note: “He will pass through it נִקְשֶׁה וְרָעֵב, hard pressed and hungry”, and curse his king and his God.

senses.definition: Of a woman giving birth: to labour with great difficulty.

evidence.note: “Rachel gave birth, וַתְּקַשׁ בְּלִדְתָּהּ, and she had hard labour in her giving birth”; she died of it (Gen 35:18).

stems.gloss: make hard, heavy, difficult; harden, stiffen (neck, heart, spirit)

senses.definition: To make a burden heavier to bear.

evidence.note: “Your father הִקְשָׁה, made hard, our yoke; now lighten (הָקֵל) it.”

senses.gloss: make difficult, ask a hard thing
senses.definition: To make a thing hard to grant or obtain.

evidence.note: To Elisha’s request for a double portion of his spirit, Elijah: “הִקְשִׁיתָ לִשְׁאוֹל, you have asked a hard thing”, granted only if he sees him taken.

senses.definition: In childbirth, to labour hard.

evidence.note: “When she was in hard labour (בְהַקְשֹׁתָהּ בְּלִדְתָּהּ), the midwife said, Do not fear.”

senses.gloss: harden, stiffen (one’s neck, heart); refuse to hear
senses.definition: To make one’s neck or heart hard: to refuse to listen and turn, holding out against Yahweh’s word; said of Israel again and again, and of the one who will not take rebuke.

evidence.note: “Circumcise the foreskin of your heart, and do not stiffen (לֹא תַקְשׁוּ) your neck any more.”
“They did not listen, and stiffened their neck like the neck of their fathers, who did not believe in Yahweh their God.”
“They did not listen to me nor incline their ear, but stiffened their neck.”
“… so as not to hear and not to receive instruction.”
“They acted proudly and stiffened their neck and did not listen to your commandments.”
They stiffened their neck and appointed a head to go back to their bondage, “but you are a God of forgiveness”.
“They gave a stubborn shoulder and stiffened their neck and would not hear.”
Hezekiah: “Do not stiffen your neck as your fathers, but give the hand to Yahweh.”
Zedekiah “stiffened his neck and hardened (וַיְאַמֵּץ) his heart from turning to Yahweh”.
“Do not harden your heart as at Meribah, as in the day of Massah in the wilderness”, quoted in Heb 3:8, 15; 4:7.
“Happy the man who fears continually, but he who hardens his heart (מַקְשֶׁה לִבּוֹ) will fall into evil.”
“A man of rebukes who stiffens the neck will suddenly be broken, and no healing.”
“Who has hardened himself against him and been whole?”
Psa 95:8 quoted: μὴ σκληρύνητε τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν; Peshitta לָא תּקַשֻּׁון.

senses.gloss: harden (another’s spirit or heart); be hard (unwilling)
senses.definition: Of Yahweh: to make a ruler’s heart or spirit hard so that he will not yield, to bring about his judgment; and of the ruler himself, to be hard and refuse.

evidence.note: “I will harden (אַקְשֶׁה) Pharaoh’s heart and multiply my signs and my wonders in the land of Egypt.”
Sihon would not let Israel pass, “for Yahweh your God hardened his spirit and made his heart strong, to give him into your hand”.
“When Pharaoh was hard (הִקְשָׁה) about letting us go, Yahweh killed every firstborn in Egypt.”

evidence.locator: קָשָׁה (hiphil) → σκληρύνω, Exo.7.3, Deu.10.16, Psa.95.8, 2Ch.30.8; (qal) Gen.49.7, 2Sa.19.44 (MACULA alignment)

evidence.note: Psa 95:8 quoted: “Do not harden your hearts as in the provocation.”
“Lest any of you be hardened by the deceitfulness of sin.”
Of Pharaoh (Rom 9:17): “He has mercy on whom he will, and whom he will he hardens.”
Some “were hardened and did not believe”, speaking evil of the Way.

words.gloss: one-piece work, beaten or turned from a solid mass of metal
words.summary: A way of making a thing of gold or silver, used of the cherubim and lampstand of the tabernacle and of the two silver trumpets: the whole worked out of one piece, its parts “from it” and not joined on. Its link to קָשָׁה “be hard” is not shown by the text: it may be work of hard, solid metal, but no verse or cognate yet ties it to the root’s sense. Jer 10:5, filed here, may instead be the homograph “field of cucumbers” (Isa 1:8).

senses.gloss: work of one piece, beaten or turned work
senses.definition: Metalwork made out of one solid piece: the lampstand with its shaft, cups, knobs and flowers all “from it”, the cherubim from the two ends of the covering, the trumpets of silver.

evidence.note: “Their knobs and their branches shall be from it; all of it מִקְשָׁה אַחַת, one piece of pure gold.”
“מִקְשָׁה the lampstand shall be made; its base and shaft, its cups, knobs and flowers shall be from it (מִמֶּנָּה).”
Two cherubim of gold, מִקְשָׁה, “from the two ends of the covering”; Exo 25:19, “from the covering you shall make the cherubim”.
“This was the work of the lampstand: מִקְשָׁה of gold, to its shaft and to its flower it was מִקְשָׁה”, after the pattern Yahweh showed Moses.
“Make two trumpets of silver; מִקְשָׁה you shall make them”, for calling the assembly and for breaking camp.

The idol, a tree cut down and decked with silver and gold, is “like a תֹּמֶר of מִקְשָׁה; they do not speak; they must be carried”: either a post of turned work or a scarecrow in a cucumber field (the homograph of Isa 1:8). The word is uncertain here.

words.summary: Used once, of Israel’s hardness, in Moses’ plea after the calf; its sense is fixed by its pairing with wickedness and sin.

senses.definition: The hardness of a people that will not yield, set beside wickedness and sin.

evidence.note: “Remember your servants Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; do not look at the קְשִׁי of this people, nor at its wickedness (רֶשַׁע), nor its sin.”

words.summary: Used once, in מַעֲשֶׂה מִקְשֶׁה, the finery of Jerusalem’s women that will become baldness. The verse shows only that it is something done to the hair; what kind of work, and how it comes from קָשָׁה, is not clear.

senses.definition: Hair worked or set in some way, the opposite of the baldness that replaces it.

evidence.note: “Instead of מַעֲשֶׂה מִקְשֶׁה, baldness (קָרְחָה)”, in a list of finery turned to shame: perfume to rot, a girdle to a rope, a robe to sackcloth.

words.summary: The Peshitta’s ܩܫܐ, for σκληρύνω: the same hardening of the heart against God’s word as the Hebrew hiphil.

senses.definition: To make the heart hard: of men against God’s voice, and of God, who hardens whom he will.

evidence.note: Psa 95:8: “Do not harden (לָא תּקַשֻּׁון) your hearts.”
“Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts.”
“On whom he will he has mercy, and whom he will he hardens (מקַשֵּׁא)”, of Pharaoh.

senses.definition: To become hard, refusing to believe.

evidence.note: “Lest any of you be hardened (נֵתקַשֵּׁא) by the deceitfulness of sin.”
Some “were hardened (מֵתקַשֵּׁין) and did not believe”, speaking evil of the way of God.

words.gloss: hard, harsh, severe; stiff (of neck, heart)
words.summary: The Peshitta’s ܩܫܝܐ, for σκληρός and other Greek words: a hard word, a hard master, hard times, fierce winds, and hearts and necks that will not bend.

senses.definition: Of a heart or neck: hard, unyielding to God.

evidence.note: “You קַשְׁיַי קְדָלָא, hard of neck, and uncircumcised in heart”: the Peshitta has the very phrase of Exo 33:5.
“Is your heart still קַשְׁיָא?”, of disciples who do not yet understand.

senses.definition: Of a word, a master, times, a wind, charges: hard to bear or to deal with.

evidence.note: “This word is קַשְׁיָא; who can hear it?”
“I knew you, that you are a hard man, reaping where you did not sow.”
“It is hard for you to kick against the goads.”
Many and grievous charges against Paul.
“In the last days hard times will come.”
Ships driven by hard winds.
Servants subject to masters, not only to the good and gentle but also to the harsh.
The hard things ungodly sinners have spoken against him.

words.summary: The Peshitta’s ܩܫܝܘܬܐ: for σκληροκαρδία and σκληρότης, the hardness of heart Jesus rebukes, and for ἀποτομία, God’s severity toward those who fell.

senses.definition: A heart that will not yield or believe.

evidence.note: “Moses, because of the קַשְׁיוּת of your heart, allowed you to put away your wives.”
Grieved at the hardness of their heart.
He rebuked their unbelief and hardness of heart.
“By your hardness and impenitent heart you store up wrath for yourself.”

senses.definition: God’s severe judgment, set against his kindness.

evidence.note: “See then the kindness and the קַשְׁיוּתָא of God: on those who fell, severity; on you, kindness, if you continue in it.”

senses.definition: Of rebuke or use of authority: with severity.

evidence.note: “Rebuke them sharply, that they may be sound in the faith.”
“That when present I may not deal sharply.”

cognates.gloss: become hard, rigid, callous; hardness, harshness, cruelty; hard, harsh; (form III) endure, struggle with the severity of
cognates.note: Arabic root q-s-w: the verb “to become hard, rigid, callous”, the noun “hardness … severity, harshness, cruelty”, the participle “hard, stiff; harsh, severe”, and form III “he endured it; struggled … with its difficulty, or severity”. Hard of substance and hard of dealing, as קָשֶׁה. Arabic s (س) answers to Hebrew שׁ from the older š; it is not ṯ (ث).

evidence.note: “He endured it; struggled, or contended, with, or against, it; … with, or against, its difficulty, or severity.”

evidence.locator: Arabic قسا (qasā); قسوة (qaswa); قاس (qāsin), root ق س و
evidence.note: “to become hard, to become rigid, to become callous”; “hardness, stiffness, rigidity; severity … harshness … cruelty”.

cognates.gloss: be hard, difficult; (aphel) harden; hard, strong, heavy, difficult
cognates.note: Jewish Aramaic: the Targums use the same root where the Hebrew has it: the verb for “too hard” (Targ. Deu 1:17; 15:18), the aphel for “harden” (Targ. Exo 7:3; Psa 95:8; 1Ki 12:4; 2Ki 2:10), and the adjective for hard service and cruel wrath (Targ. Exo 6:9; Gen 49:7).

s.v. קָשֵׁי, קַשְׁיָא I (adj.), citing Targ. Ex. VI, 9; Gen. XLIX, 7; Is. XIX, 4; Ps. LX, 5

cognates.note: Syriac root qšʾ. The Peshitta New Testament uses its words, which are given as words of the entry.

doctrine.statement: At the calf Yahweh says of Israel, “it is עַם קְשֵׁה עֹרֶף” (Exo 32:9), and will not go up among them lest he consume them (Exo 33:3, 5); yet Moses asks him to go among them on that very ground, “for it is a stiff-necked people; pardon our iniquity” (Exo 34:9). Moses tells them the land is given “not for your righteousness, for you are a stiff-necked people” (Deu 9:6), pleads that Yahweh not look at their קְשִׁי but remember Abraham, Isaac and Jacob (Deu 9:27), and commands, “Circumcise the foreskin of your heart and do not stiffen your neck any more” (Deu 10:16). Later generations “stiffened their neck like the neck of their fathers, who did not believe in Yahweh” (2Ki 17:14; Jer 7:26; Neh 9:16–17, 29), and Yahweh remained “a God of forgiveness” (Neh 9:17). Stephen sums up the history in the same words: “You stiff-necked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, you always resist the holy spirit; as your fathers did, so do you” (Act 7:51). From the verses: the hard neck is the people’s own refusal to hear, it is joined to unbelief, and what Israel received it received for the fathers’ sake and by Yahweh’s forgiveness, not its own righteousness; the cure is a circumcised heart.

Yahweh says, “I will harden (אַקְשֶׁה) Pharaoh’s heart and multiply my signs” (Exo 7:3), and he hardened Sihon’s spirit “to give him into your hand” (Deu 2:30); yet the same history says Pharaoh “was hard about letting us go” (Exo 13:15), and Yahweh tells Pharaoh he was raised up to show his power (Exo 9:16). Israel is warned, “Do not harden your heart as at Meribah” (Psa 95:8); “he who hardens his heart will fall into evil” (Pro 28:14), and “he who, often rebuked, stiffens his neck will suddenly be broken” (Pro 29:1). Paul, citing Pharaoh, writes that God “has mercy on whom he will, and whom he will he hardens” (Rom 9:17–18), and Hebrews takes Psa 95:8 as a warning to believers: “Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts”, “lest any of you be hardened by the deceitfulness of sin”, for that generation could not enter “because of unbelief” (Heb 3:7–8, 13, 15, 19; 4:7). From the verses: scripture says both that God hardens and that men harden themselves; the hardening God sends falls on men already set against him, to bring about his judgment and show his power, and the warning to every hearer is to hear his voice while it is called today.

note: Left out: קִשְׁיוֹן (s.ds.ad), Kishion, a Levitical town of Issachar (Jos 19:20; 21:28): a place, so no name entry. יָשְׁבְּקָשָׁה, Joshbekashah son of Heman (1Ch 25:4, 24), may contain קָשָׁה but was not asked for here. מִקְשָׁה “field of cucumbers” (Isa 1:8, s.dq.ac) is of קשא, from קִשֻּׁאָה “cucumber”, and belongs there; Jer 10:5 is filed under this root’s מִקְשָׁה and may be that word instead (a scarecrow in a cucumber field). Greek: the Septuagint renders מִקְשָׁה by τορευτός, στερεός and ἐλατός, none used in the New Testament of this work, so not recorded; Deu 9:27 קְשִׁי is σκληρότης in the Septuagint (Rom 2:5 uses it), but MACULA leaves the word unaligned, so it is not cited. Leads not yet followed: Lane’s main article قسو (form I قَسَا, of hearts, Qur’an 2:74) is missing from the vendored data, which has only قَاسَاهُ; Payne Smith’s page for ܩܫܐ; Ge'ez and Akkadian (no clear qšw/qšy “hard” found in the vendored Oracc glossaries). The Peshitta’s קַשְׁיָא (Mat 14:30, Act 27:18) of a strong wind was not cited.
